overview: White offers the e-pawn at once with 2.e4, a move-order trick related to the Alekhine-style attack on an advanced knight. After 2...Nxe4 White plays 3.Qe2 or 3.Nc3 for quick development, hoping for a lead in development against Black's centralised knight. Black can keep the pawn and neutralise by returning it, so White's compensation is thin.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nc3, Qe2 and d3 to harass the e4 knight

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4, retreat the knight (...Nf6 or ...Nc5) and return the pawn for a safe, equal position

typical_structures.structure: White a pawn down with an open e-file and development lead

character.notes: White gives a pawn and plays for tricks; I expect sharp, tactical play, but I am unsure of the lines.

gambit.notes: 2...Nxe4 can be kept if Black avoids the early traps.

soundness.notes: Strong players regard it as unsound for White; scores through surprise.

structure.notes: Centre cleared on the e-file; open lines.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.notes: Dubious so not Beginner; intermediate by default.

character.reason: A pawn sacrificed for early initiative; forcing play.
